body: July-Sept 2012: Intel, TSMC and Samsung took a combined 23% stake in ASML for €3.85bn and committed €1.38bn to EUV and 450mm R&D (customer co-investment program; Intel ~15%, TSMC 5%, Samsung 3%). ASML also bought Cymer (light source) in 2012-13. EUV took until ~2017-19 to reach volume production; ASML is the only supplier, enabling 7nm and below. ADR ~$49 (July 2012, Intel investment date) -> ~$172 (Oct 2018, +350%) -> peak ~$1,100 (July 2024) [unverified] ≈ 22x plus dividends. Split [approx]: EPS ~€2.6 (2012) -> ~€19 (2024) ≈ 7x; P/E ~20x -> ~40x ≈ 2x. Drawdowns: ~-59% (Nov 2021-Oct 2022) and ~-45-50% (July 2024-2025) on China export curbs and order softness [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible in 2012: the three largest chipmakers paying billions for equity to make sure EUV got built — customers voting with capital for a single-source chokepoint. Samsung's retained stake reportedly grew ~17x. Who caught it: the customers themselves (TSMC sold out 2015, Intel/Samsung trimmed from 2016 — leaving most of the gain on the table). LESSON: when customers co-fund a supplier's monopoly technology, the moat is being built in public; the payoff took 5-7 years of technical risk and the stock stays cyclical (-50% swings) even as a monopoly.

data.lesson: customer co-investment = public moat signal; monopolies stay cyclical
data.who_caught_it: customers (Intel, TSMC, Samsung) — most sold early

title: ASML 2012-2024: EUV monopoly co-funded by its customers, ~22x
